question: Why can a consistent formal system not prove all true statements?
answer: Some statements are true but cannot be proven inside a consistent formal system. Proving such a statement would mean proving a falsehood, which a consistent system cannot do. By numbering every symbol, Gödel showed that any strong enough system can say this about itself.
move: Any consistent system of maths leaves some truths unprovable.
